verses.1: Job continued his resolve and said:
verses.2: By the living God who has removed my judgment, and by the Almighty who has made my life bitter,
verses.3: as long as my breath is in me and the breath of God is in my nostrils,
verses.4: if my lips were to speak falsehood, and if my tongue were to utter deceit,
verses.5: may it be far from me to justify you! Until I die, I will not deny my integrity.
verses.6: By my righteousness I hold fast, and I will not let go. My heart will not accuse me all my days.
verses.7: Let my enemies be like the wicked, and my adversaries like the unrighteous.
verses.8: What is the hope of the wicked, that he would gain? When God takes his life, will he do so?
verses.9: Will He hear his cry when trouble comes to him?
verses.10: Will he find favor with the Almighty when he calls on God at all times?
verses.11: I will teach you what is in the hand of God, what is with the Almighty I will not conceal.
verses.12: Indeed, you have all seen it—why then are you so full of empty talk?
verses.13: This is the portion of the wicked man with God, and the inheritance of the wicked from the Almighty:
verses.14: If his children multiply, they will fall by the sword, and his descendants will not be satisfied with bread.
verses.15: His survivors will be buried in death, and his widows will not weep.
verses.16: If he gathers silver like dust, and piles up clothing like clay,
verses.17: he may heap it up, but the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide the silver.
verses.18: He builds his house like a moth’s home and like a booth erected by a watchman.
verses.19: The rich will lie down and not be gathered—his eyes open and he is no longer there.
verses.20: Terrors will overtake him like waters, and a storm will steal him away in the night.
verses.21: The east wind will carry him off and he will go, and the storm will uproot him from his place.
verses.22: It will cast him out and have no mercy. From his hand he will flee.
verses.23: It will strike him with its hands, and tear him away from his place.

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: "the breath of God is in my nostrils" follows the Hebrew phrase נַפְשִׁי in the sense of "life" or "self," not "soul."
- v. 11: "in the hand of God" refers to what God holds or reveals, not to divine power or control.
- v. 23: "strike him with its hands" is a vivid metaphor for divine punishment; the Hebrew uses כַפֵּימוֹ ("their hands") to refer to the agent of destruction.
raw:
[1] Job continued his resolve and said:

[2] By the living God who has removed my judgment, and by the Almighty who has made my life bitter,

[3] as long as my breath is in me and the breath of God is in my nostrils,

[4] if my lips were to speak falsehood, and if my tongue were to utter deceit,

[5] may it be far from me to justify you! Until I die, I will not deny my integrity.

[6] By my righteousness I hold fast, and I will not let go. My heart will not accuse me all my days.

[7] Let my enemies be like the wicked, and my adversaries like the unrighteous.

[8] What is the hope of the wicked, that he would gain? When God takes his life, will he do so?

[9] Will He hear his cry when trouble comes to him?

[10] Will he find favor with the Almighty when he calls on God at all times?

[11] I will teach you what is in the hand of God, what is with the Almighty I will not conceal.

[12] Indeed, you have all seen it—why then are you so full of empty talk?

[13] This is the portion of the wicked man with God, and the inheritance of the wicked from the Almighty:

[14] If his children multiply, they will fall by the sword, and his descendants will not be satisfied with bread.

[15] His survivors will be buried in death, and his widows will not weep.

[16] If he gathers silver like dust, and piles up clothing like clay,

[17] he may heap it up, but the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide the silver.

[18] He builds his house like a moth’s home and like a booth erected by a watchman.

[19] The rich will lie down and not be gathered—his eyes open and he is no longer there.

[20] Terrors will overtake him like waters, and a storm will steal him away in the night.

[21] The east wind will carry him off and he will go, and the storm will uproot him from his place.

[22] It will cast him out and have no mercy. From his hand he will flee.

[23] It will strike him with its hands, and tear him away from his place.

Notes
- v. 3: "the breath of God is in my nostrils" follows the Hebrew phrase נַפְשִׁי in the sense of "life" or "self," not "soul."
- v. 11: "in the hand of God" refers to what God holds or reveals, not to divine power or control.
- v. 23: "strike him with its hands" is a vivid metaphor for divine punishment; the Hebrew uses כַפֵּימוֹ ("their hands") to refer to the agent of destruction.
